title: Cross-task, explainable and real-time decoding of human emotion states by integrating gray and white matter intracranial neural activity
methods: personalized deep-learning regression of continuous affect
frequency-domain power density of decoded time series vs random-decoding null

data_sources: in-house stereo-EEG (iEEG) recordings with simultaneous self-rated valence/arousal

data_scope.primary_cohort: 18 individuals with clinically implanted intracranial electrodes
data_scope.tasks: 2 emotion-eliciting paradigms (affective video task, affective image task)
data_scope.target_variables: continuous self-rated valence and arousal (Russell circumplex axes)
data_scope.signal_type: iEEG from both gray-matter and white-matter contacts, multi-band spectral features (gamma band strongest single band)
data_scope.not_stated_in_accessible_text: per-subject contact counts, sampling rate, total trial/rating counts, exact decoding correlation values, network architecture details (main text and Methods are subscription-gated)
data_scope.supplementary: Figs. 1-28, Tables 1-11, Notes 1-8, Video 1 (real-time decoding demo)
data_scope.data_availability: restricted clinical data; minimum de-identified dataset on reasonable request to corresponding author (response within 4 weeks); source data XLSX provided for Figs. 2-5 and Extended Data Figs. 2-5
data_scope.recording_site: Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China

core_conclusion: Personalized deep-learning decoders on intracranial EEG track continuous valence and arousal above the performance of prior EEG and iEEG work, and the decisive gain comes from integrating white-matter signals with gray-matter signals rather than discarding white-matter contacts. The models generalize across two structurally different emotion-eliciting tasks, expose shared and preference-specific mesolimbic-thalamo-cortical subnetworks that make the decoding neurophysiologically explainable, and run robustly in real time in four new individuals - moving affective BCIs toward deployable closed-loop therapeutic systems.
why_it_matters: Rehabilitates routinely discarded white-matter iEEG contacts as genuine affect signal, raising the usable channel yield of existing clinical archives; delivers accuracy, cross-context generalization, anatomical explainability and real-time operation in one cohort rather than one at a time; decodes continuous circumplex states that a closed-loop therapy controller can act on; and demonstrates prospective online deployment in four new individuals, with clinical stakes in treatment-resistant affective disorders.
why_nature: Nature Computational Science favours computational frameworks that themselves yield biological insight - here decoder attribution becomes a claim about mesolimbic-thalamo-cortical circuit organization. Generalization and explainability are treated as first-class results rather than accuracy leaderboards; the human iEEG-plus-dense-affect dataset is rare and expensive; deployment is demonstrated prospectively rather than promised; and two Extended Data tables benchmark the advance against the whole prior iEEG emotion/mood decoding literature.
added_value_to_my_research: Anatomy-as-token pretraining -> geography-as-token geospatial foundation models with few-shot new-city fine-tuning curves
Tract-constrained physics-informed GNN -> road/transit-network graph decoders reading mid-link observations for flow and service-area models
Neurally-decoded valence/arousal -> physiological gold standard for calibrating greenspace and urbanicity exposure-response curves
Conditional-shift transferability index -> a priori cross-city transfer score, reframing MGWR non-stationarity as locally measured domain shift
Streaming state estimation with calibrated uncertainty -> online spatiotemporal KDE and live efficiency-equity service allocation, linked to 2SFCA mental-health accessibility
